result.method: Batched JSON-RPC reads pinned to the block hash (EIP-1898); EIP-1967 / EIP-1822 / beacon proxies; capabilities from PUSH4 selectors in proxy + implementation bytecode (heuristic).
result.summary: No owner(), admin() or authority() and getRoleMemberCount reverted, but the bytecode exposes grantRole / setAuthority (PUSH4 heuristic): role-based admin is likely and was not resolved; inspect it before relying on it. Capabilities seen in bytecode: upgrade.

assessment.method: Live bytecode + storage heuristic at the pinned block only: this contract is not in Pacta's indexed catalog (no documentation comparison).
limits: riskScore (0-100) is a heuristic of the controller type and of pause / blacklist / upgrade capabilities read at one block; it is not an audit.

The live check reads EIP-1967 slots, owner(), Safe getThreshold() / getOwners() and TimelockController getMinDelay(); custom role systems, bridge or L2 admin paths and off-chain operations are not resolved.
Documentation is compared only for indexed protocols (catalogMatch), at their pinned block.

result.coverage_gap_hint: Target is not yet indexed or fully classified. Ask the user if they want you to queue coverage or request this capability via pacta_submit_request (free community queue, or 24h priority clearance for issuers).

upgrade_x402.note: Free tier: 50 pre-flight calls per caller per UTC day (REST and MCP), then $0.01 per call over x402 (HTTP 402, never a dead-end 429). Paid routes below: POST the JSON body with an x402 X-PAYMENT (v1) or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2) header.

endpoints.unlocks: fast contract / token control-plane verdict: riskScore 0-100, grade A-F, upgrade / owner / pause / blacklist / mint flags and a shareable scan URL
full control-plane dossier: every controller Safe's signers and threshold, signers shared with other indexed protocols, Base EAS proof
pre-signing calldata check: timelock / Safe / multicall calls decoded, each rated against live delays and the authority that governs it
deep control-plane scan cross-checked on two independent RPC operators, auditor receipt and a queued Base EAS ticket

pinnedDualRpcChainProof.officialDeploymentBinding: https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/omnibridge/overview links to https://github.com/Near-One/omni-bridge whose README Contract Addresses table lists Ethereum Mainnet Bridge Contract 0xe00c629aFaCCb0510995A2B95560E446A24c85B9; evm/src/omni-bridge/contracts/OmniBridge.sol enforces onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) on _authorizeUpgrade, pause, upgradeToken, and admin bridge configuration, and onlyRole(PAUSABLE_ADMIN_ROLE) on pauseAll.
pinnedDualRpcChainProof.note: Mismatch summary: NEAR Omni Bridge official documentation (https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/omnibridge/overview and https://docs.near.org/chain-abstraction/omnibridge/implementation) claims trustless cross-chain transfers secured by Chain Signatures (2/3+ MPC nodes) and the Ethereum/NEAR light client, with no mention of any upgradeable proxy, multisig admin, or EOA pause key across Omni Bridge docs or SECURITY.md. On-chain at finalized Ethereum block #26448541, the official mainnet OmniBridge UUPS ERC1967Proxy (0xe00c629aFaCCb0510995A2B95560E446A24c85B9, holding $14.5M+ USDC) grants DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (controlling _authorizeUpgrade / upgradeToAndCall and bridge parameters) directly to a 3-of-5 Safe (0x2468603819Bf09Ed3Fb6f3EFeff24B1955f3CDE1) with 0s timelock delay, and grants PAUSABLE_ADMIN_ROLE to a single EOA (0xd9cb077700aa4d32d30bda5e99bb171549b5a382).

docsQuote: It solves key challenges in cross-chain communication by leveraging Chain Signatures and its decentralized Multi-Party Computation (MPC) service to enable trustless cross-chain asset transfers.
